title: Book One · Chapter 129: A Bag Full of Stones
story:
Mum puts six clean stones in the blue bag.

Ronan looks at them, then at her.

“Are we eating those?”

“Only if the rice is gone.”

Dad laughs from the doorway. He has just come home. He puts his work things down. Then he touches the bag.

Mum asks him to lift it. He carries it across the yard and back. Then she lifts it herself. One handle pulls against her fingers.

“Too narrow,” she says.

“It holds,” Dad says.

“It hurts.”

He gives the handle back to her. She lays it flat on the table and opens her hand. There is a thin red line across her fingers.

Ronan remembers the long handles of the moving cart. His hands had red marks that day too. He puts his own hand beside Mum's. It is larger than it was then. It is still much smaller than hers.

“Can the handle be wider?” he asks.

“I will try wider handles.”

Dad takes the stones out. He makes a little row on the ground with them. Ronan picks up one and draws a circle around it in the dust.

“A whole shop for stones,” Dad says.

“No customers yet.”

“You need a sign.”

Ronan gives him the smallest stone. “You can be the first.”

Dad pays with a leaf. Then he asks for change. Ronan tears the leaf in half and gives one piece back. Mum laughs and puts her needle down. She cannot sew and laugh so hard at once.

The next evening she has two wider handles ready. She puts the stones in again. This time she asks Ronan to lift only one side while she holds the other. They carry it to the door together.

“Better,” she says.

“Can I draw the stones in your picture?”

“You can draw us testing the bag.”

Dad tests the wider handles too. He carries the bag in one hand, then the other. Mum tells him to walk as far as the gate, not just across the kitchen.

Ronan walks beside him. He still has the leaf from their game. Outside, Mr Qiu asks, “What have you bought?”

“Six very good stones,” Dad says.

“My pencils are lighter.”

They come back with the same six stones. Mum writes a short note for herself on the back of a paper. She writes: These wider handles work well. Then she writes a note about the next change. Ronan watches her check the handles again.

At school Mei looks at his new drawing. Mum and Ronan have the bag between them. Six round shapes sit in the bottom.

“They look like eggs,” Mei says.

“They are stones.”

“Did you carry them very carefully?”

“They did not break.”

She asks Ronan, then changes one drawn stone. She makes its edge a little rough. It looks heavier at once. Ronan changes the others himself.

He writes the words under the picture at home. Mum reads them, changes one line, and says yes to the classroom wall. She points to his line about the bag. “Do not write NEVER BREAKS,” she says. They have only tried this one.

He takes out “never.” He writes “so far” on the back. He will ask Miss Wu, “How can I use SO FAR?”

When the picture goes up, Leo studies it.

“You are carrying money,” he says.

“Stones.”

“My father takes money when we go away. Then Mum buys clothes. He says the clothes fill our bags.”

Ronan thinks about that all the way home. His bag is full of schoolbooks. Mum's is still hers, and the stones are back beside the pot.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：tests / testing＝试用、测试；narrow＝窄；so far＝到目前为止。

情节提示：handle＝提手；wider＝更宽的；rough edge＝粗糙的边缘。

理解：1. “结实”为什么还不足以说明袋子好用？2. Mum 为什么不允许写“永远不会坏”？
